classification.difficultyReason: Directly applies the taught graphical and boundary-comparison tests: distinguish holes and jumps from connected corners, identify a marked vertical asymptote, and compare adjacent formulas at each boundary. Checking two boundaries does not require a new method.

content.prompt: State the values of $x$ at which a discontinuity occurs.

spec.description: Black piecewise graph with a hole at x=3 and separate open and closed endpoints at x=4. Unlabelled heights are schematic drawing positions, not additional numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Horizontal segment y=2 joins a rising segment at x=1; the two middle segments meet at an excluded point at x=3; a jump occurs at x=4.
spec.answerVisibility: Question graph only; discontinuity locations are not annotated.

answer.worked: At $x=3$, the graph has a hole. At $x=4$, the open endpoint and filled endpoint have different heights. The discontinuities occur at $x=3$ and $x=4$.

spec.description: Black connected segments through filled points at x=2 and x=5, followed by separate open and closed endpoints at x=7. Unlabelled heights are schematic drawing positions, not additional numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: The graph joins at x=2 and x=5 but has a jump at x=7.
spec.answerVisibility: Question graph only; no answer annotation.

answer.worked: At $x=7$, the open endpoint and filled endpoint have different heights, so the pieces do not join. The discontinuity occurs at $x=7$.

spec.description: Two blue reciprocal-shaped branches, blue dashed vertical asymptote at x=2, and black axes with arrows at both ends. No grid or other numerical scale is supplied.
spec.mathematics: Branches are below the x-axis to the left of x=2 and above it to the right. The plotting model represents the source shape; no equation is asserted as a given.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph and asymptote only; no answer annotation.

answer.worked: The graph has a vertical asymptote at $x=2$, where the function is undefined. The discontinuity occurs at $x=2$.

At the boundary $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}3(0)&=0\\-2(0)+2&=2\end{aligned}$$
The values differ, so the pieces do not join. The discontinuity occurs at $x=0$.

At $x=-1$:
$$\begin{aligned}-(-1)&=1\\(-1)^2&=1\end{aligned}$$
The pieces join at $x=-1$.

At $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0^2&=0\\-3(0)+1&=1\end{aligned}$$
The values differ, so the only discontinuity occurs at $x=0$.

At $x=1$, the first formula gives $2$, while
$$\begin{aligned}(1-4)^2-9&=9-9\\&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The pieces do not join at $x=1$.

At $x=7$:
$$\begin{aligned}(7-4)^2-9&=0\\7-7&=0\end{aligned}$$
The pieces join at $x=7$. The only discontinuity occurs at $x=1$.
